title: What Does an Amazon Virtual Assistant Do? Tasks and Duties
tags: amazon virtual assistant, amazon va, virtual assistant tasks, amazon fba virtual assistant, amazon seller va
description: What an Amazon virtual assistant does day to day: the tasks, duties and roles of an Amazon VA, the types of VA, and which work to keep for yourself.
content:
An Amazon virtual assistant (Amazon VA) is a remote professional who handles the operational work of an Amazon seller account. They work inside Seller Central on your behalf: updating listings, answering buyer messages, creating FBA shipments, tracking inventory, following up Seller Support cases and reporting back to you. A good Amazon VA takes the daily, repeatable work off your desk so you can spend your time on products, suppliers and growth.

This guide covers what an Amazon virtual assistant actually does, the different roles a VA can take, the duties to hand over first, and the work you should keep for yourself.

What is an Amazon virtual assistant?

A virtual assistant is someone who supports a business remotely. An Amazon virtual assistant is a VA who specialises in Amazon selling. The difference matters. A general virtual assistant manages email, calendars and admin. An Amazon VA knows how Seller Central works, how FBA inventory moves, what Amazon's policies allow, and which small problems turn into expensive ones if nobody spots them.

Most Amazon VAs work for private label brands, wholesalers and resellers on Amazon FBA, FBM or both. Some work alone as freelancers. Others, like the assistants at XpertVA, work inside a team with specialists behind them.

What does an Amazon VA do? The core tasks

The exact task list depends on your account, but most Amazon virtual assistant tasks fall into eight groups.

1. Listing management

Creating new listings, uploading flat files, fixing variation families, updating images and bullets, adding backend search terms, and fixing suppressed or stranded listings. Listing errors are one of the most common reasons a product quietly stops selling, so this is usually the first duty sellers hand over.

2. Customer service

Answering buyer messages inside Amazon's 24 hour response expectation, processing returns and refunds, handling A-to-z guarantee claims with evidence, and following up on product questions. Fast, polite replies protect your seller metrics and your reviews.

3. FBA shipments and inventory

Building shipment plans, preparing box content information, booking carriers, and checking that every unit is received at the fulfilment centre. An Amazon FBA virtual assistant also watches stock levels against restock limits and lead times, so you are warned before you run out.

4. Seller Support cases

Opening cases, escalating them when the first answer is wrong, and chasing them until they close. Many cases end without a resolution simply because nobody followed up.

5. Account health monitoring

Checking the Account Health dashboard, policy warnings, intellectual property complaints and performance notifications every day, and flagging anything serious to you the same day.

6. Reimbursements

Finding units Amazon lost or damaged, returns that were refunded but never came back, and fee overcharges, then filing claims inside Amazon's claim windows.

7. Research

Gathering competitor prices, mining reviews for product problems, and building keyword lists in tools such as Helium 10. The VA collects and organises the information. You, or a specialist, make the decision.

8. Reporting

A weekly summary of sales, ad spend, open issues and what needs your decision. The best reports are short and written in plain language.

A typical week for an Amazon seller VA

WhenTask
Every morningBuyer messages, returns, account health check, suppressed listings
DailyFollow up open Seller Support cases
Twice a weekInventory levels against restock limits
WeeklyFBA shipments, listing updates, competitor and review checks, report to you
MonthlyReimbursement audit and claims

Types of Amazon virtual assistant

Not every VA does everything. When you hire, it helps to know which role you actually need.

  • General Amazon VA: listings, messages, cases and admin. The right first hire for most sellers.
  • Amazon FBA virtual assistant: focused on shipments, inventory planning and reimbursements.
  • Customer service VA: buyer messages, returns and reviews, often across several marketplaces.
  • Listing and content VA: listing creation, copy updates and image coordination.
  • PPC assistant: search term reports, negative keywords and bid changes under a PPC manager's direction.
  • Research VA: product, competitor and keyword research to support sourcing decisions.

Virtual assistant duties: what to hand over first

Start with work that is frequent, rule-based and easy to check. A sensible order is:

  1. Buyer messages and returns
  2. Suppressed and stranded listing fixes
  3. Seller Support case follow-up
  4. FBA shipment creation and receipt checks
  5. Weekly reporting

Once the VA has handled those well for a few weeks, add listing updates, inventory planning and reimbursements.

What an Amazon VA should not do

Some work should stay with you or a specialist, at least at first:

  • Changing bank, tax or payment settings
  • Writing a suspension appeal on their own
  • Setting your pricing strategy or advertising budget
  • Agreeing terms with suppliers on your behalf

Keep your VA on their own secondary user in Seller Central with only the permissions their tasks need. Never share your primary login.

Skills a good Amazon VA needs

  • Hands-on experience in Seller Central, including flat files and case logs
  • Working knowledge of Amazon policies and FBA requirements
  • Clear written English for buyer messages and reports
  • Attention to detail, because small listing errors are expensive
  • Comfort with common tools such as Helium 10, spreadsheets and shared task boards

If you are writing a role description, our Amazon VA job description template lists the duties and skills in full.

Do you need an Amazon virtual assistant?

You probably do if you recognise two or more of these:

  • You spend more of your week on Seller Central admin than on growth
  • Buyer messages or cases slip when you are busy or away
  • You have lost sales to suppressed listings or stockouts you noticed late
  • You have never audited your FBA reimbursements

title: How to Hire an Amazon Virtual Assistant in 2026
tags: hire amazon virtual assistant, amazon va, virtual assistant agency, best virtual assistant, amazon expert for hire
description: How to hire an Amazon virtual assistant: freelancer vs agency, what affects cost, questions to ask, red flags, and how to run a safe first month.
content:
Hiring an Amazon virtual assistant can give you back hours every week, or cost you months and a damaged account if you pick the wrong one. This guide explains how to choose an Amazon VA service: the main options, what drives the cost, the questions to ask, the red flags to avoid, and how to run the first month safely.

Start with the work, not the hire

Before you look at any Amazon virtual assistant service, write down the tasks you want to hand over and how often they happen. For example: buyer messages every morning, FBA shipments weekly, reimbursements monthly. This list tells you how many hours you need, what experience the VA must have, and how you will know if they are doing a good job.

If you are not sure what to include, our guide to what an Amazon virtual assistant does lists the common tasks and duties.

Your three options

1. A freelance VA from a marketplace

Freelance sites let you hire an individual directly. It can be the cheapest route and works well for simple, low-risk tasks. The trade-offs: experience varies a lot, there is no cover when they are away, and you are responsible for training, checking work and replacing them if it does not work out.

2. A virtual assistant agency

A virtual assistant agency employs and manages the assistants. You pay more than a freelancer, but you get vetting, cover for absence and someone accountable if things go wrong. Check whether the agency specialises in Amazon or supplies general assistants who will need training.

3. An Amazon specialist with dedicated VAs

Some firms, including XpertVA, provide dedicated Amazon VAs backed by in-house specialists in PPC, listings and account health. This suits sellers who want one named assistant but also need expert help for the harder problems.

FreelancerGeneral VA agencyAmazon specialist
Amazon experienceVariesOften limitedCore skill
Cover for absenceNoYesYes
Training needed from youHighMedium to highLow
Specialist back-upNoRarelyYes
Best forSimple tasksGeneral adminGrowing Amazon brands

What affects the cost of an Amazon VA

Searching for the cheapest virtual assistant usually costs more in the end, because mistakes in Seller Central are expensive. Cost depends on:

  • Hours: part-time cover costs less than a full-time dedicated VA.
  • Experience: a VA who already knows Seller Central and FBA costs more per hour but needs far less of your time.
  • Management: agencies include vetting, cover and supervision in the price.
  • Scope: several marketplaces, a large catalogue or specialist tasks add hours.

For a wider comparison of offshore and in-house costs, see virtual assistant cost in 2026.

Questions to ask before you hire an Amazon virtual assistant

  1. Which Amazon accounts and categories have you worked on, and for how long?
  2. How will you access Seller Central? (The only right answer is their own secondary user.)
  3. Who covers the work when you are away?
  4. What will you send me each week?
  5. Can you show a sample report, or walk me through how you handle a stranded listing?
  6. What happens if it is not working out?
  7. Who do you go to when a problem is beyond you, such as an account suspension?

Red flags

  • Asking for your main Seller Central login or password
  • Vague answers about Amazon experience
  • Promises of guaranteed rankings or sales figures
  • No written scope of work
  • No plan for cover or replacement
  • Suggesting review manipulation or other tactics that break Amazon's rules

How to run the first 30 days

  1. Week 1: set up a secondary user with limited permissions. Share your processes and a short catalogue overview.
  2. Week 2: hand over two or three low-risk, frequent tasks, such as buyer messages and suppressed listings.
  3. Week 3: review their first reports. Check a sample of their work directly in Seller Central.
  4. Week 4: if the work is accurate and on time, add shipments, cases or inventory tracking.

By the end of the month you should know whether the VA saves you time. If you are spending as many hours checking their work as you used to spend doing it, the hire is not working.

How to tell if your Amazon VA is working

  • Buyer messages are answered inside 24 hours
  • Suppressed and stranded listings are fixed within a day or two
  • Cases are followed up until they close
  • You get a clear report every week without asking
  • You are spending noticeably less time in Seller Central

title: Amazon VA Job Description: Duties and Skills Template
tags: amazon virtual assistant job description, amazon va job description, virtual assistant responsibilities, virtual assistant duties, virtual assistant skills
description: A ready-to-use Amazon VA job description: responsibilities, required skills, tools, weekly duties and how to measure performance. Copy and adapt it.
content:
A clear job description is the fastest way to hire the right Amazon virtual assistant. It tells candidates exactly what the role involves, gives you a fair way to compare them, and becomes the checklist you use to judge their work later. Below is a ready-to-use Amazon VA job description you can copy and adapt, followed by notes on each section.

Amazon virtual assistant job description template

Role summary

We are an Amazon seller looking for an experienced Amazon virtual assistant to manage the day-to-day operations of our Seller Central account. You will handle listings, customer messages, FBA shipments, inventory tracking, Seller Support cases and weekly reporting, working remotely during agreed hours.

Key responsibilities

  • Create, update and maintain product listings, including flat file uploads, variations, images and backend search terms
  • Monitor and fix suppressed, stranded and inactive listings
  • Respond to buyer messages within 24 hours and process returns and refunds
  • Prepare responses and evidence for A-to-z guarantee claims
  • Create FBA shipment plans, prepare box content and track receipts
  • Monitor inventory against restock limits and flag reorder points
  • Open, escalate and follow up Seller Support cases until they close
  • Check Account Health daily and report warnings the same day
  • Identify and file reimbursement claims for lost or damaged inventory
  • Gather competitor, review and keyword data when requested
  • Send a written weekly report covering tasks completed, issues and decisions needed

Required skills and experience

  • At least one year working in Amazon Seller Central for a seller or agency
  • Experience with FBA shipments, flat files and the case log
  • Good working knowledge of Amazon selling policies
  • Clear, professional written English
  • Strong attention to detail and a habit of checking your own work
  • Reliable internet connection and availability during agreed hours

Nice to have

  • Experience with Helium 10 or similar Amazon research tools
  • Experience across more than one Amazon marketplace
  • Basic understanding of Amazon PPC reports
  • Experience on Walmart, Shopify or eBay

Tools you will use

Amazon Seller Central, spreadsheets (Google Sheets or Excel), our task board, our team chat, and Amazon research tools as needed.

How performance is measured

  • Buyer messages answered within 24 hours
  • Suppressed listings fixed within two working days
  • No avoidable stockouts
  • Cases followed up until closed
  • Weekly report delivered on time

Working arrangement

Remote, [part-time / full-time], [hours and time zone]. Access is through your own Seller Central user with permissions limited to your tasks.

Notes on each section

Be specific in the responsibilities

"Manage our Amazon account" attracts everyone and filters no one. Listing the actual virtual assistant duties, such as flat files, FBA shipments and case follow-up, means candidates can tell honestly whether they have done the work before.

Separate must-have skills from nice-to-have

Seller Central experience is a must. Tool experience can be taught. Keeping the required list short stops good candidates ruling themselves out.

Put the measures in the job description

Writing down how performance is measured sets expectations from day one and gives you an objective way to review the first month. It is the part most Amazon seller job descriptions leave out.

State the access rules up front

Saying that the VA will have their own limited user, never your main login, attracts professionals and puts off anyone who expects full control.

Virtual assistant skills summary

If you only remember one thing: the best Amazon VAs combine hands-on Seller Central experience, clear writing and careful checking. Ask candidates to describe how they would fix a stranded listing or chase a case Amazon closed without solving. The quality of that answer tells you more than any CV.

How to use this template

  1. Delete any responsibilities you will not hand over in the first three months.
  2. Fill in hours, time zone and marketplaces.
  3. Add a short practical test, such as rewriting one of your listing bullets or drafting a reply to a difficult buyer message.
  4. Use the performance measures as the agenda for your 30-day review.
